title: GPU failure-mode injection and resilience playbook
author: Ethan Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood's recommended approach for intentional failure-mode injection (chaos) across GPU fleets and attached networking to validate resilience, alerting, and automated remediation. It covers safe experiment design, Terraform/IaC adapters for fault injection, CI/CD gating, telemetry queries to detect failure fingerprints, and step-by-step recovery runbooks.

Scope:
- Applies to all production and staging GPU clusters (on-prem and cloud) managed by eng-infra.
- Focus areas: node preemption/failure, NVLink/interconnect degradation, driver/kernel hangs, disk/network egress impairment, scheduler starvation, and KV-cache rehydration failure modes.
- Excludes customer VPCs deployed via Private (customer-managed networks) unless approved through security review.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Validate end-to-end SLO preservation mechanisms under common failure modes. Target: no more than 1 P50 latency spike > 2x baseline and no more than 0.1% error-rate delta for critical routes (model inference) during controlled experiments.
- Ensure automated fallback policies (model variant, region fallback, queue draining) trigger correctly.
- Verify alert fidelity: high-confidence alerts fire for true positives and no more than one false-positive per 10 experiments.

Ownership and cadence:
- Experiment owner: eng-infra resilience squad.
- Stakeholders: serving-runtime, eng-sre, oncall, product (for customer-impact review).
- Recurring cadence: safety-approved chaos window every two weeks for non-prod; quarterly for production with ticketed customer communication.

Experiment design checklist (must pass before run):
1) Safety review completed and increment ID recorded.
2) Rollback and stop-playbook tested in staging.
3) Impact blast-radius scoped (percentage of nodes, tenant whitelist).
4) Oncall and PagerDuty routing notified with runbook link.
5) Canary traffic profile and synthetic probes configured.
6) Metrics and tracing dashboards annotated for the run.

Failure-mode categories and example injections:
- Node preemptions: orchestrate evictions (cloud spot termination API or local dramageddon shim). Example command (GCP):
  gcloud compute instances simulate-maintenance --instance=INSTANCE --zone=ZONE
- GPU driver hang: load a synthetic kernel with forced segfault into driver path on a single node. Use safety harness only.
- NVLink degradation: add 10–20% packet loss on the interconnect fabric in lab via iptables/netem on select hosts.
- Network egress shaping: tc qdisc netem delay/limit to simulate egress congestion for a tenant subnet.
- Disk I/O saturation: fio job with 80% bandwidth for 5m on a node local disk to observe scheduler eviction behavior.

Terraform / IaC adapters for controlled injection:
- Pattern: provide small Terraform modules that toggle a 'chaos' deployment (daemonset or operator) with a safe boolean flag and a label selector for target pools. The module must:
  - accept percentage_of_nodes (string, e.g. "10%")
  - accept target_tags (list of strings)
  - expose a "dry_run" toggle for CI gating
  - require approver list (string)

Example interface (module variables in HCL — example):
  variable "percentage_of_nodes" { type = string description = "10% or 3" }
  variable "target_tags" { type = list(string) default = ["chaos-safe"] }
  variable "dry_run" { type = bool default = true }

Usage snippet (CLI):
  terraform apply -var='percentage_of_nodes=5%' -var='dry_run=false' 

CI/CD integration and gating:
- Non-prod experiments are triggered by a Jenkins/Buildkite pipeline named infra-chaos-runner. Pipeline stages: plan -> dry-run -> gated-approval -> run -> collect -> analyze.
- Production experiments require: documented business justification, executive signoff, and an oncall runbook owner pinned to PagerDuty for the window.
- PR checks for GPU runtime changes must include a default chaos-safety matrix in the PR description.

Telemetry queries and fingerprints (examples):
- High-level metrics to monitor during a run:
  - job.evictions.count by tenant (alert if > baseline + 5/min)
  - inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 per model route (spike detection)
  - node.gpu.utilization and node.gpu.thermal (unexpected drop patterns)
  - kvcache.miss_rate and kvcache.rehydration_time
  - host.network.tx_errors and netem_packet_loss

Example PromQL alerts (text):
  - name: GPUNodeEvictionSpike
    expr: increase(job_evictions_total[5m]) > 20
  - name: ModelLatencyRegression
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) > (baseline_95 * 2)

Automated remediation patterns (priority order):
1) Automatic local restart and driver reload for single-node driver hangs (safely scoped).
2) Scheduler-level soft-drain: divert new requests to warm pool, allow in-flight requests to finish, then cordon node.
3) Regional fallback: route traffic to compatible model variant in alternative region (if latency budget allows).
4) Tenant backoff policy: apply exponential backoff token to noisy tenants.

Manual recovery playbook (step-by-step):
1) Identify the signature (use telemetry fingerprints above).
2) If node driver hang: SSH to node via bastion, run: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver || sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia. If restart fails, cordon node and trigger reprovision.
3) If KV-cache rehydration failures: trigger background seeding job: kubectl apply -f kvcache-seed-job.yaml --namespace=platform-eval. Monitor kvcache.rehydration_time metric.
4) If network egress shaping observed: remove netem rule and validate egress-pings to 8.8.8.8 and model-serving endpoints.
5) For multi-node NVLink issues: escalate to hardware and fleet teams; open ticket with hardware logs (dmesg, /var/log/nvlink.log).

Safety and blast-radius controls (required):
- Default max-impact: 5% of nodes per AZ, not exceeding 10 nodes in small clusters.
- Tenant whitelisting: experiments cannot target tenants with active enterprise contracts during production windows.
- Auto-abort conditions:
  - System-wide error rate > 0.5% sustained for 3m.
  - P99 latency > 2x baseline sustained for 2m.
  - Any security control or KMS key rotation triggered.

Post-mortem and observability checklist (after each experiment):
- Annotate dashboards and archive synthetic probe traces.
- Produce a 1-page experiment summary: scope, injection, observed vs expected, automated remediation success, lessons learned, follow-ups.
- Update telemetry fingerprints and SLO baselines if necessary.
- If automation failed, file an action with owning team and a deadline for remediation.

Runbook snippets and templates (copyable):
- Emergency abort (one-line):
  ./infra-chaos-runner abort --experiment-id=EXP-2025-001 --reason="auto-abort-triggered"

- Staging quick-reset (YAML job to drain and reprovision one node):
  apiVersion: batch/v1
  kind: Job
  metadata:
    name: node-reset-job
  spec:
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: reset
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl cordon ${NODE} && kubectl drain ${NODE} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data && terraform taint module.gke_node.${NODE} && terraform apply -auto-approve"]
        restartPolicy: Never

Testing and validation matrix (table, plain text):
- Test type | Environment | Blast-radius | Success criteria
- Driver hang injection | staging | 1 node | driver restarts without manual reprovision and inference p95 within 1.5x baseline
- NVLink packet loss | lab | 2 nodes | model correctness intact; KV-cache miss increase < 10%
- Spot preemption storm | canary-prod | 5% nodes | auto-fallback triggers and no customer 1xx/5xx spike > 1%

Appendix: artifact locations and CLI references:
- Terraform chaos module repo: git@github.com:redwood-infra/terraform-chaos-modules.git
- Buildkite pipeline: infra/chaos-runner (team: eng-infra)
- Dashboards: Observability -> "Resilience / GPU Chaos"
- PagerDuty escalation: eng-infra-resilience -> primary oncall
